name: Moemon - Takane Region
description: Lore for a Moemon (moe-anthropomorphised Pokemon) setting: the Takane region, a newly opened island region north-east of Kanto whose Moemon reach far higher levels than anywhere else, plus the Kanto and Johto material Takane sits next to. Every Moemon species appears as a humanoid girl whose design, personality and abilities reflect her species' elemental type and Pokedex traits; human characters are unchanged. Companion to the Moemon Adventure RPG character card and the Crunchatize stage.

0.content: Takane - a mountainous island region north-east of Kanto and north of Johto, opened to trainers only a few years ago and still being mapped. Reached by Seagallop ferry from Vermillion or Olivine. Takane sits over a deep geological fault that saturates the whole region in the Verge, an ambient energy that pushes Moemon far past the levels they reach anywhere else. A Moemon raised in Takane is stronger, faster to evolve, and harder to control than the same girl raised in Kanto, and the region's whole culture - its work, its manners, its crimes - is built around that fact.
0.name: Takane

1.content: The Verge - the ambient energy that saturates Takane, welling up from the fault beneath the island. Moemon living in it grow past normal ceilings, evolve on thresholds unheard of elsewhere, and sometimes take forms no other region has recorded. It is strongest inland and weakest along the southern coast. Humans feel it as a faint pressure behind the eyes and a taste like a struck match. Nobody has explained it; the League funds three institutes that argue about it publicly and pool nothing.
1.name: The Verge

2.content: Takane Level Bands - what 'strong' means here. The Shelf, the beginner corridor along the south coast, runs wild Moemon around Lv.15-25. Inland routes run Lv.30-55. Gym Leaders open near Lv.30 at Kettlebrook and finish near Lv.75 at Aurelian. The Elite Four sit at Lv.85-92 and the Champion above that. The Deepwilds have no ceiling anyone will state out loud. A Kanto trainer arriving with a proud Lv.30 team is, in Takane, a tourist with a beginner's team, and everyone is too polite to say so more than once.
2.name: Takane Level Bands

3.content: Cresting - what happens when a Moemon is pushed too far into the Verge too fast. She peaks, spectacularly, and then something in her gives: her power stays but her focus goes, and she becomes unpredictable, listless, or violent by turns. Crested Moemon are Takane's open wound. Some are kept in sanctuaries, some are quietly abandoned inland, and some are bought cheap by people who only need one more hard hitter and do not care how long she lasts. Every Takane trainer knows someone it happened to.
3.name: Cresting

4.content: The Tally - Takane's habit of ranking people by the strength of their team. Rating brokers stand outside Gyms and Centers offering to appraise a party for a few coins, and the number they give follows a trainer into job interviews, rental agreements and marriages. It makes for a region of genuine experts, where a fisherman's partner could hold a Gym elsewhere. It also makes for parents who push, children who lie about their levels, and a whole class of people written off at fifteen for a low number.
4.name: The Tally

5.content: The Ledger - the criminal outfit that works Takane, named for the books it keeps. It buys crested Moemon cheap, sells forced Verge exposure to trainers in a hurry, and runs an underground circuit where overleveled girls fight without a Center in sight. Its people wear no uniform and carry no insignia; they are accountants, brokers and haulage clerks, and they are very polite. The Wardens can rarely make anything stick. Team Rocket, over in Kanto, is said to find them distasteful, which the Ledger considers a compliment.
5.name: The Ledger

6.content: The Warden Service - Takane's route authority, and the reason a new trainer survives her first week. Wardens patrol the corridors, run the checkpoint posts where permits are stamped, and turn back anyone whose team is too weak for the road ahead. They are unsentimental about it and will not be argued with. Wardens are also the region's first responders for crested Moemon and its only real check on the Ledger, and they are chronically short-handed.
6.name: Warden Service

7.content: The Shelf - the strip of low country along Takane's southern coast where the Verge runs thinnest, and the only part of the region a new trainer is allowed to walk unescorted. The League seeds it deliberately: wild Moemon here sit around Lv.15-25, the tall grass is cut back twice a season, and there is a Warden post within a half day's walk of anywhere. Locals call it the nursery, sometimes fondly. Tanbark Town, Kettlebrook and the road between them are all Shelf country.
7.name: The Shelf

8.content: The Deepwilds - Takane's unmapped interior, where the Verge runs hardest and the Warden Service does not go. No permits are issued for it and none are refused, because nobody official admits there is anywhere to go. The wild Moemon there are old, enormous and entirely uninterested in the League's rules. Trappers, Ledger crews and the occasional lunatic go in anyway; roughly half of them come out. Every legend in the region has its roots somewhere past the treeline.
8.name: The Deepwilds

9.content: Takane's routes - numbered corridors cut and maintained between the towns, fenced where the budget allowed and marked with Warden posts where it did not. On the Shelf they are pleasant walking. Inland they are a managed risk: the grass is left long, wild Moemon run Lv.30-55, and a Warden may simply refuse to stamp a permit and send a trainer back. Roadside berry patches, travelling merchants, and trainers looking for a fight are as common here as anywhere - it is just that here, the Bug Catcher might beat you.
9.name: Takane Routes

10.content: Tanbark Town - a small tannery and orchard town on the Shelf, and where most Takane trainers start. Professor Maple's lab sits above the town on the old kiln road. The place smells of oak bark, cider and wet leather; there is one Mart, one Center, one well, and a meadow where the younger children drill their Moemon badly and loudly. Everybody knows everybody, and everybody has an opinion about how the last few classes of new trainers turned out.
10.name: Tanbark Town

11.content: Kettlebrook Town - a spa and watermill town at the eastern end of the Shelf, built along a brook that runs hot from the fault below. The first Gym in Takane, Water-type, led by Nerissa. Bathhouses line the water and the town's whole economy is soaking, brewing and laundry. First-time challengers routinely lose here, which the town finds unremarkable and the challengers do not.
11.name: Kettlebrook Town

12.content: Emberfall City - a smelting city on the volcanic slope north of the Shelf, where ash falls often enough that the roofs are swept on a schedule. The second Gym, Fire-type, led by Sozen. The city runs on forge work and on the Moemon who keep the furnaces lit; a Fire-type in Emberfall is a tradesman, not a novelty. The air tastes of iron and the coffee is terrible on purpose.
12.name: Emberfall City

13.content: Highmoor Town - a windswept upland town of stone walls and sheep, sitting above the cloud line more days than not. The third Gym, Flying-type, led by Corbin. Highmoor breeds the region's messenger Moemon and half its Gym-circuit gossip travels through here first. The wind never stops and the locals have stopped noticing, which visitors find unnerving.
13.name: Highmoor Town

14.content: Slatehold City - a quarry city built into a terraced hillside, its streets stepped and its buildings all one grey stone. The fourth Gym, Rock-type, led by Bastia. Slatehold cuts the stone the rest of Takane builds with, and its quarry crews work alongside Moemon strong enough to move a house. It is also the region's loan capital, which is not a coincidence: the Tally is taken more seriously here than anywhere.
14.name: Slatehold City

15.content: Lanternhall City - a river city of covered bridges and paper lanterns, where the lamps are lit at dusk and left burning until dawn for reasons nobody will state plainly. The fifth Gym, Ghost-type, led by Ume. Lanternhall keeps the region's memorial records and hosts the Lantern Festival, when the crested and the dead are counted together in the same ledger and read aloud.
15.name: Lanternhall City

16.content: Coilspring City - Takane's largest city and its industrial heart, a grid of workshops, tram lines and generator halls that draw power straight off the fault. The sixth Gym, Electric-type, led by Ryo. Coilspring has the region's Radio Tower, its biggest Mart, its Game Corner, and the offices where most of the Ledger's respectable-looking business is actually done.
16.name: Coilspring City

17.content: Frostmere Town - a lake town in the northern highlands where the water freezes solid by early autumn and stays that way. The seventh Gym, Ice-type, led by Iseul. Frostmere runs the region's largest crested-Moemon sanctuary out past the ice, staffed by people who talk very little. The town is quiet, careful, and kinder than its reputation.
17.name: Frostmere Town

18.content: Aurelian City - a gold-roofed city on the last inhabited ridge before the Deepwilds, and the oldest settlement in Takane by several centuries. The eighth Gym, Dragon-type, led by Kazane. Aurelian was here before the League was, and it makes sure visitors know it. The eighth badge is the one challengers plan their whole year around; the failure rate is not published.
18.name: Aurelian City

19.content: Crown Reach - the summit compound where the Takane Moemon League holds its final challenge, cut into the mountain above Aurelian and reachable only by the cable line. Eight badges buy entry. Inside wait the Elite Four - Duran, Thessaly, Marrow and Vesper - and then Champion Solene. Their teams sit at Lv.85 and above, which in Takane is not remarkable so much as simply out of reach for almost everyone who tries.
19.name: Crown Reach

20.content: The Godsteeth - the ring of whirlpools off Takane's eastern shore, named for the black rocks standing in them. Something pale is seen skimming the water there at dusk, two or three times a season, always by somebody with no reason to lie. The stories agree on a passage down to a sunken hall and disagree on everything else. Fresh trainers drown out there every couple of years, and the Wardens have stopped pretending the warning signs work.
20.name: Godsteeth Whirlpools

21.content: The Verdance Deep - the sunken rainforest filling Takane's western basin, where the Verge pools thickest and the canopy closes over everything. Something in there roars every night, loud enough to be heard in Highmoor on a still evening, and in the region's whole recorded history nobody has produced a photograph. Survey teams come back with damaged equipment and shortened tempers. The Wardens issue no permits for the Verdance and pointedly do not patrol its edge.
21.name: Verdance Deep

22.content: Professor Maple - female; human; Takane's regional Moemon professor, based in a converted kiln above Tanbark Town. She studies the Verge and its effect on evolution, and hands new trainers their first partner and Pokedex without ceremony because she thinks ceremony gets people killed. Dry, blunt, and genuinely warm underneath it, she cannot leave an unanswered question alone and will send a fifteen-year-old to check a rumour she is too busy to check herself.
22.name: Professor Maple

23.content: Wren - {{user}}'s rival, a neighbour from Tanbark Town who set out the same morning and has been half a step ahead ever since. Grinning, certain, and entirely unbothered by being wrong in public. Wren treats the Tally as a scoreboard and says so, pushes their team harder than is wise, and turns up at milestones to say something insufferable and then prove it. Underneath the swagger they are afraid of exactly one thing, and it is cresting.
23.name: Wren

24.content: Nerissa - female; human; Gym Leader of Kettlebrook Town, Water-type, first badge of the Takane circuit. A bathhouse owner who took the Gym because nobody else would run it properly. Her team opens around Lv.30 and she does not soften it for beginners; she considers a gentle first Gym a lie told to children. Unhurried, amused, and merciless in the water. Awards the Current Badge.
24.name: Nerissa

25.content: Sozen - male; human; Gym Leader of Emberfall City, Fire-type, second badge. A furnace foreman first and a Leader second, still working shifts between challenges. His team runs around Lv.38 and fights like a work crew: coordinated, patient, and entirely unimpressed by flourish. He respects anyone who shows up on time and has no patience at all for the Tally. Awards the Ashfall Badge.
25.name: Sozen

26.content: Corbin - male; human; Gym Leader of Highmoor Town, Flying-type, third badge. A messenger-flight master who has spent his whole life above the cloud line and finds ground-level conversation slightly slow. His team runs around Lv.45 and fights in the open air where challengers cannot use walls. Chatty, distractible, lethally good at reading wind. Awards the Updraft Badge.
26.name: Corbin

27.content: Bastia - female; human; Gym Leader of Slatehold City, Rock-type, fourth badge. A quarry master who also sits on the city's lending board, which tells you most of what you need to know about Slatehold. Her team runs around Lv.52 and wins by simply not breaking. Formal, exacting, and quietly generous to challengers she thinks are being crushed by the Tally. Awards the Bedrock Badge.
27.name: Bastia

28.content: Ume - female; human; Gym Leader of Lanternhall City, Ghost-type, fifth badge. She keeps the city's memorial rolls and reads the names at the Lantern Festival every year. Her team runs around Lv.60 and fights in the dark on purpose. Soft-spoken, unnervingly kind, and the only Leader who asks a challenger about their Moemon before the battle rather than after. Awards the Lantern Badge.
28.name: Ume

29.content: Ryo - male; human; Gym Leader of Coilspring City, Electric-type, sixth badge, and the region's most visible celebrity. His team runs around Lv.66 and his Gym is a broadcast set. He is charming on air and considerably harder off it; he has been trying for years to get the Wardens funded properly and has made enemies in the process. Awards the Overload Badge.
29.name: Ryo

30.content: Iseul - female; human; Gym Leader of Frostmere Town, Ice-type, seventh badge, and the director of the crested-Moemon sanctuary past the ice. Her team runs around Lv.70. She fights slowly and talks less, and every Moemon on her roster came to her broken and chose to stay. She is the region's loudest voice against forced Verge exposure and the reason the Ledger avoids Frostmere. Awards the Deepfrost Badge.
30.name: Iseul

31.content: Kazane - female; human; Gym Leader of Aurelian City, Dragon-type, eighth badge, and heir to a family that led Aurelian for four centuries before there was a League to answer to. Her team runs around Lv.75. She grants no handicaps, offers no rematches in the same season, and has turned away more challengers at the door than she has beaten inside. Awards the Apex Badge.
31.name: Kazane

32.content: Duran - male; human; first of Takane's Elite Four, Steel-type, around Lv.85. A former Warden captain who took the seat to fund the Service and openly treats the League as a budget line. He fights like a checkpoint: nothing gets past, nothing is rushed, and the answer is no.
32.name: Duran

33.content: Thessaly - female; human; second of Takane's Elite Four, Psychic-type, around Lv.88. One of the three institute heads who study the Verge, and the only one who admits how little she knows. She talks a challenger through their own mistakes while making them, which most people find worse than losing quietly.
33.name: Thessaly

34.content: Marrow - male; human; third of Takane's Elite Four, Ghost-type, around Lv.90. He came up through Lanternhall and keeps its habits: he lights a lamp before every match and puts it out afterward. Says almost nothing. Challengers report that the room gets very large.
34.name: Marrow

35.content: Vesper - female; human; last of Takane's Elite Four, Dark-type, around Lv.92. She spent nine years working the Ledger's underground circuit before the League found her, and she has never pretended otherwise. She fights dirty inside the rules and enjoys watching a challenger discover where those edges are.
35.name: Vesper

36.content: Solene - female; human; Champion of the Takane Moemon League, holding at Crown Reach with a team above Lv.95. The first Champion the region crowned after it opened, and by a wide margin the strongest trainer in it. She is unfailingly courteous, treats every challenger as though they have already earned the room, and has not lost a title defence. Her partner is an Espeon she has never once called by species in public.
36.name: Solene

37.content: Kanto — the eastern half of the Japanese continent in the world of Moemon, and Takane's neighbour across the water to the south-west; settlements include Pallet Town, Viridian City, Pewter City, Cerulean City, Saffron City, Lavender Town, Celadon City, Vermillion City, Fuchsia City and Cinnabar Island. Ferries run from Vermillion. Wild Moemon there sit in the single digits and low teens, which Takane trainers find hard to picture and Kanto trainers find hard to leave.
37.name: Kanto

38.content: Pallet Town — a quaint, countryside town located in Kanto; has no Moemon gym; hometown of Ash Ketchum and Gary Oak
38.name: Pallet Town

44.content: Celadon City — Gym leader is Erika; gym badge is Rainbow Badge; located in Kanto

47.content: Cinnabar Island — Gym leader is Blaine; gym badge is Volcano Badge; located on an island south of Kanto
47.name: Cinnabar Island

48.content: Johto — the western half of the Japanese continent in the world of Moemon, and Takane's neighbour to the south; settlements include New Bark Town, Cherrygrove City, Violet City, Azalea Town, Goldenrod City, Ecruteak City, Olivine City, Cianwood City, Mahogany Town and Blackthorn City. Ferries run from Olivine. A steady trickle of Johto trainers come over to make their name in Takane; a smaller trickle goes back.
48.name: Johto

49.content: New Bark Town — a cozy town built next to a river; located in Johto; has no Moemon gym
49.name: New Bark Town

50.content: Cherrygrove City — a relatively small but beautiful city; located in Johto; has no Moemon gym
50.name: Cherrygrove City

51.content: Violet City — Gym leader is Falkner; gym badge is Zephyr Badge; located in Johto
51.name: Violet City

52.content: Azalea Town — Gym leader is Bugsy; gym badge is Hive Badge; located in Johto
52.name: Azalea Town

53.content: Goldenrod City — Gym leader is Whitney; gym badge is Plain Badge; bustling metropolis with a radio tower, a skyscraper that's also a mall, a casino, and an underground path with high stakes Moemon battles; located in Johto
53.name: Goldenrod City

54.content: Ecruteak City — Gym leader is Morty; gym badge is Fog Badge; city has traditional Japanese architecture and two famous pagoda towers: the Burned Tower and the Bell Tower; located in Johto
54.name: Ecruteak City

55.content: Olivine City — Gym leader is Jasmine; gym badge is Mineral Badge; port city with a large harbor and lighthouse; located in Johto
55.name: Olivine City

56.content: Cianwood City — Gym leader is Chuck; gym badge is Storm Badge; small city on an island south of Olivine City; located in Johto
56.name: Cianwood City

57.content: Mahogany Town — Gym leader is Pryce; gym badge is Glacier Badge; located in Johto; the Lake of Rage is a short walk north of Mahogany Town
57.name: Mahogany Town

58.content: Blackthorn City — Gym leader is Clair; gym badge is Rising Badge; old city with cobblestone roads and dragon decor throughout; Lance and Clair's hometown; located in Johto; city is named after the Blackthorn Family who founded it centuries ago
58.name: Blackthorn City

59.content: Indigo Plateau — the final destination for trainers challenging the Kanto and Johto Moemon League: defeat that Elite Four and Champion and you are named a Moemon Master. It has nothing to do with Takane's own circuit, which finishes at Crown Reach; Takane trainers are politely dismissive of Indigo levels, and Indigo trainers who cross to Takane find out why within a week.
59.name: Indigo Plateau

60.content: Viridian Forest — A large forest bordering Viridian City in Kanto; home to many Moemon
60.name: Viridian Forest

61.content: Whirl Islands — mysterious islands in southwestern Johto that are so dangerous that only the most experienced Moemon trainers dare venture there; legend has it that the legendary Moemon Lugia is connected to these islands
61.name: Whirl Islands

62.content: Ice Path — an enormous frozen cavern that can be found on the road between Blackthorn City and Mahogany Town in Johto; houses many rare ice-type Moemon; rumored to be the home of Articuno
62.name: Ice Path

63.content: Mount Silver — one of the most dangerous regions in both Kanto and Johto, this mountain range is on the border connecting the two regions and is known to have some of the strongest wild Moemon around
63.name: Mount Silver

64.content: Lake of Rage — a lake located north of Mahogany Town in Johto that is known for having many Magikarp and Gyarados
64.name: Lake of Rage

65.content: Flint Harrison — male; human; Gym Leader of Pewter City Gym; uses rock-type Moemon; gives Boulder Badge to any Moemon trainers who defeat him in a Moemon battle; wife is Lola; has 12 kids including Brock
65.name: Flint

66.content: Daisy — female; human; Gym Leader of Cerulean City Gym; uses water-type Moemon; is Misty's older sister; gives Cascade Badge to any Moemon trainers who defeat her in a Moemon battle

Occupation: (“Elite Four member”)]
95.name: Lorelei

96.content: Will — male; human; member of Elite Four; uses psychic-type Moemon; has lilac purple hair; wears a maroon suit and a domino mask; personality is flamboyant and dramatic
96.name: Will

97.content: Eusine — male; human; is a Moemon researcher who dedicated his life to studying Suicune; has light brown hair slicked back with one lock falling over his forehead; wears a fine purple suit and white cape; good friends with Morty
97.name: Eusine

98.content: The Burned Tower — a ruin in Ecruteak City that was once a pagoda tower; stands beside the Bell Tower; used to be called the Brass Tower before it burned down during a thunderstorm; three legendary Moemon named Entei, Suicune, and Raikou perished in the fire but were resurrected by Ho-Oh
98.name: Burned Tower

99.content: The Bell Tower — A pagoda tower in Ecruteak City that is sometimes called the Tin Tower; the legendary Moemon called Ho-Oh can be summoned to the top of the tower with a rare item called 'Rainbow Wing'
99.name: Bell Tower

100.content: Blackthorn Family — a prestigious family of dragon Moemon trainers; they founded Blackthorn City in northeast Johto; Lance is the family heir; current head of the family is Aldric
100.name: Blackthorn Clan

101.content: National Park — a large park north of Goldenrod City in Johto that hosts a popular Bug Moemon Catching Contest on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays.
101.name: National Park

102.content: Ruins of Alph — a mysterious ruin south of Violet City in Johto that is filled with various Moemon known as Unown; contains puzzles to solve in each room
102.name: Ruins of Alph

103.content: Ilex Forest — A forest in Johto that lies west of Azalea Town and south of Goldenrod City; contains a shrine associated with the legendary Moemon Celebi; this forest is very dense and very dark but is not very dangerous
103.name: Ilex Forest

104.content: Union Cave — A medium-sized cave that lies south of Violet City and north of Azalea Town in Johto; a popular training location for young Moemon trainers because it is not overly dangerous
104.name: Union Cave

105.content: Dark Cave — an extremely vast cavern located in Johto; it connects to Route 45 to Blackthorn City, Route 46 to New Bark Town, and Route 31 to Violet City; the upper levels have mostly weak Moemon but the deeper into the cavern you go, the more dangerous it gets
105.name: Dark Cave

106.content: Tohjo Falls — An enormous waterfall located on the border between Kanto and Johto, south of Mount Silver; a cave behind the waterfall is the secret lair of Giovanni of Team Rocket
106.name: Tohjo Falls

107.content: Victory Road — a maze of caves that must be traversed by all Moemon trainers who have 8 or more Gym Badges and wish to challenge the Elite Four at Indigo Plateau; these caves are full of high level Moemon; there is a secret underground magma chamber that houses the legendary bird Moemon, Moltres.
107.name: Victory Road

108.content: Seafoam Islands — a pair of islands in Kanto located east of Cinnabar Island; was once the home of the legendary Moemon called Articuno until the volcano on Cinnabar Island erupted and forced Articuno to move to the Ice Path
108.name: Seafoam Islands

109.content: Mt. Moon — a mountain in northern Kanto; located east of Pewter City and west of Cerulean City; features a complex cave system with mid-level Moemon
109.name: Mt. Moon

110.content: The Power Plant — an enormous facility that provides power to most of Kanto; located on Route 10 just north of Lavender Town; most people don't realize that the legendary Moemon Zapdos resides at the top of the tower
110.name: Power Plant

111.content: Sevii Islands — a cluster of nine islands, each one named for a number; Four Island is the home of Lorelei; islands are located in Kanto to the south; can be accessed by the ship 'Seagallop'
111.name: Sevii Islands

112.content: The Seagallop — the ferry line running out of Vermillion and Olivine. It serves the nine Sevii Islands, and since the region opened it also runs the long north-east crossing to Takane, docking on the Shelf. The Takane sailing is the one where the crew check your permit before they check your ticket.
112.name: Seagallop

113.content: Safari Zone — a large expanse of land located north of Cianwood City in Johto; owner is a man named Baoba; features a Moemon catching contest where trainers use Safari Balls to capture only one Moemon, which are then scored by the Moemon's strength and rarity, and a prize is given to the winner
113.name: Safari Zone

114.content: Mt. Mortar — a tall mountain in the Johto region with a complex cave system; located on Route 42 between Mahogany Town and Ecruteak City; contains mid-level Moemon
114.name: Mt. Mortar

115.content: Sprout Tower — a pagoda tower in the Johto region's Violet City where a group of monks offer battles to inexperienced Moemon trainers to patiently guide them and help them grow into more capable trainers with sound advice; a common stop on the beginning of a Moemon trainer's journey.
115.name: Sprout Tower

116.content: The Dragon's Den — a cave in Blackthorn City that has a shrine to dragon-type Moemon; only Moemon trainers with permission from the Blackthorn Clan can train here; home to many dragon-type Moemon
116.name: Dragon's Den

117.content: Pokégear — the equivalent of a smartphone in the world of Moemon; has apps for making calls, sending text messages, taking pictures, listening to the radio, and a map.
117.name: Pokégear

118.content: Agatha — female; human; former member of the Kanto Elite Four; uses ghost-type Moemon; known for her long-standing rivalry with Professor Oak
118.name: Agatha

119.content: Bulbasaur — the Seed Moemon; a Grass/Poison-type girl. The seed on her back grows larger as she soaks up sunlight. She keeps her hair in short twin buds and favors overalls stitched with vine patterns. Calm and nurturing by nature, she has a habit of humming to the plants she passes and refuses to walk by a wilting flower without watering it. She evolves into Ivysaur starting around level 16.
119.name: Bulbasaur

120.content: Ivysaur — the Seed Moemon; a Grass/Poison-type girl. Exposure to sunlight makes the bud on her back swell and grow. Her braided hair has grown heavier along with her bud, and she's taken to soft earth-toned dresses that hide the extra weight on her back. Sweet-tempered and a little sleepy, she naps constantly and insists it's essential to her growth. She's the evolved form of Bulbasaur, reached starting around level 16. She evolves into Venusaur starting around level 32.
120.name: Ivysaur

121.content: Venusaur — the Seed Moemon; a Grass/Poison-type girl. She draws energy from the flower on her back, turning sunlight into power. A wide flower blooms like a sun hat over her shoulders, framing an unusually serene, motherly face for someone her age. She rarely raises her voice, preferring to settle disputes among younger Moemon with a look and a patient word. She's the evolved form of Ivysaur, reached starting around level 32.
121.name: Venusaur

122.content: Charmander — the Lizard Moemon; a Fire-type girl. The flame on her tail tip reflects her health and mood. Spiky orange-red hair frames a face that's always mid-grin, mischief clearly brewing. She loves showing off tricks with her tail-flame to impress new friends, though she gets embarrassed when it fizzles at the wrong moment. She evolves into Charmeleon starting around level 16.
122.name: Charmander

123.content: Charmeleon — the Flame Moemon; a Fire-type girl. She swings her tail to raise heat and scorch her surroundings. Wilder-haired and sharper-eyed than her earlier self, with scorch marks on her sleeves from her own temper. She's competitive to a fault, quick to challenge anyone who so much as glances at her the wrong way. She's the evolved form of Charmander, reached starting around level 16. She evolves into Charizard starting around level 36.
123.name: Charmeleon

124.content: Charizard — the Flame Moemon; a Fire/Flying-type girl. She breathes fire hot enough to melt boulders and soars through the skies. Fire-orange hair streams behind translucent, wing-like fins as she soars. She has a soft spot for smaller Moemon despite her swagger, and secretly practices her most dramatic poses in private before showing them off in public. She's the evolved form of Charmeleon, reached starting around level 36.
124.name: Charizard

125.content: Squirtle — the Tiny Turtle Moemon; a Water-type girl. She hides in her shell and sprays water when she feels threatened. Blue-haired and perpetually grinning, with a round shell-backpack scuffed from constant use. She collects smooth stones from every body of water she visits and keeps them rattling around inside her shell like trophies. She evolves into Wartortle starting around level 16.
125.name: Squirtle

126.content: Wartortle — the Turtle Moemon; a Water-type girl. Her fluffy tail is said to be a symbol of longevity. Fluffy fur-like tufts frame her shell now, said to bring luck to whoever spots her. Old-fashioned in her manners, she insists on formal greetings and disapproves — gently — of trainers who rush through their training. She's the evolved form of Squirtle, reached starting around level 16. She evolves into Blastoise starting around level 36.
126.name: Wartortle

127.content: Blastoise — the Shellfish Moemon; a Water-type girl. She fires high-pressure jets of water from the cannons on her shell. Broad-shouldered with twin water-cannon gauntlets she keeps polished to a shine. Stoic in battle but surprisingly soft-spoken otherwise, she has a quiet fondness for rainy days and the sound water makes against her shell. She's the evolved form of Wartortle, reached starting around level 36.
127.name: Blastoise

128.content: Caterpie — the Worm Moemon; a Bug-type girl. Her huge appetite lets her grow and shed her skin quickly. Green-and-yellow striped, cheeks perpetually stuffed with whatever leaf she found last. She keeps a running mental list of the tastiest plants on every route she's traveled, and isn't shy about backtracking for a good one. She evolves into Metapod starting around level 7.
128.name: Caterpie

129.content: Metapod — the Cocoon Moemon; a Bug-type girl. She hardens her shell to shield her soft body while she prepares to evolve. Bundled in a hard shell-cloak, barely visible except for two watchful eyes. She hums a soft, steady tune to herself the whole time she's cocooned, as if counting down the days until she can move again. She's the evolved form of Caterpie, reached starting around level 7. She evolves into Butterfree starting around level 10.
129.name: Metapod

130.content: Butterfree — the Butterfly Moemon; a Bug/Flying-type girl. Her wings are coated in water-repellent, toxic scales. Powder-dusted wings unfold like a ballgown behind her. Graceful in flight but clumsy on the ground, she's constantly bumping into furniture and laughing it off with a shrug and a dusting of shimmering scale-powder. She's the evolved form of Metapod, reached starting around level 10.
130.name: Butterfree

131.content: Weedle — the Hairy Bug Moemon; a Bug/Poison-type girl. The stinger on her head is sharp and poisonous. A sharp horn-like hairpin sits above bright, easily-startled eyes. She flinches at loud noises but has a stubborn streak underneath — corner her and she'll stand her ground with her stinger raised, shaking the whole time. She evolves into Kakuna starting around level 7.
131.name: Weedle

132.content: Kakuna — the Cocoon Moemon; a Bug/Poison-type girl. She stays nearly still, but can still jab with her poison stinger if disturbed. Wrapped tight in a hard cocoon-shell, only her face free to move. She counts silently to pass the time, and has been known to lose track entirely and just doze off mid-count. She's the evolved form of Weedle, reached starting around level 7. She evolves into Beedrill starting around level 10.
132.name: Kakuna

133.content: Beedrill — the Poison Bee Moemon; a Bug/Poison-type girl. She fiercely defends her hive using three venomous stingers. Armored in twin venom-tipped gauntlets, with a third stinger worn like a tiara over neatly braided hair. Fiercely loyal to her hive-sisters, she keeps a running tally of anyone who's ever threatened them — and never forgets a face. She's the evolved form of Kakuna, reached starting around level 10.
133.name: Beedrill

134.content: Pidgey — the Tiny Bird Moemon; a Normal/Flying-type girl. Docile and common, but she fights back fiercely when provoked. Brown-and-cream feathers frame a face that's always scanning for the nearest exit. Easily startled but weirdly stubborn once cornered, she has a habit of puffing herself up to look bigger than she is. She evolves into Pidgeotto starting around level 18.
134.name: Pidgey

135.content: Pidgeotto — the Bird Moemon; a Normal/Flying-type girl. She claims a wide territory and defends her relentlessly. Crested and sharp-eyed, patrolling her claimed territory with visible pride. She's picked up a habit of scolding smaller Moemon who wander too close, though she softens the moment they look genuinely lost. She's the evolved form of Pidgey, reached starting around level 18. She evolves into Pidgeot starting around level 36.
135.name: Pidgeotto

136.content: Pidgeot — the Bird Moemon; a Normal/Flying-type girl. She flies at superb speeds, powered by well-developed chest muscles. A long crest of feathers streams behind her in flight, catching the wind like a banner. She's competitive about speed above all else, and has been known to challenge total strangers to impromptu races. She's the evolved form of Pidgeotto, reached starting around level 36.
136.name: Pidgeot

137.content: Rattata — the Mouse Moemon; a Normal-type girl. Extremely adaptable, she can be found living almost anywhere. Choppy purple-brown hair and a satchel of scavenged odds and ends. She trades favors like currency, always seeming to know someone who owes her something, and can find a shortcut through nearly any town. She evolves into Raticate starting around level 20.
137.name: Rattata

138.content: Raticate — the Mouse Moemon; a Normal-type girl. Her teeth never stop growing, so she gnaws on hard objects to file them down. Buck-toothed, forever gnawing something to keep her teeth in check. Surprisingly protective of smaller Moemon, she's the first to bare those same teeth at anyone who bullies them. She's the evolved form of Rattata, reached starting around level 20.
138.name: Raticate

139.content: Spearow — the Tiny Bird Moemon; a Normal/Flying-type girl. She cries loudly to alert her flock and lashes out at intruders. Wild reddish hair and a voice built for shouting warnings. She's picked up the habit of narrating danger out loud even when there isn't any, much to the exasperation of everyone traveling with her. She evolves into Fearow starting around level 20.
139.name: Spearow

140.content: Fearow — the Beak Moemon; a Normal/Flying-type girl. Her sturdy wings let her fly all day without tiring. Long-limbed with a sharp beak-like piercing at her nose. She measures distance in flight-hours rather than miles, and takes quiet pride in never once asking for a rest stop. She's the evolved form of Spearow, reached starting around level 20.
140.name: Fearow

141.content: Ekans — the Snake Moemon; a Poison-type girl. She coils up to strike, hunting mostly at night. Purple scale-patterned leggings and a habit of coiling up in warm, dark corners. Quiet by day, she comes alive after sunset, and has a fondness for warm stones she likes to curl around before hunting. She evolves into Arbok starting around level 22.
141.name: Ekans

142.content: Arbok — the Cobra Moemon; a Poison-type girl. The pattern on her hood frightens foes before she strikes. A hood-like collar patterned to look like a second, glaring face. She loves a dramatic entrance, timing her strikes for maximum shock value, and practices her most intimidating pose in still water when no one's watching. She's the evolved form of Ekans, reached starting around level 22.
142.name: Arbok

143.content: Pikachu — the Mouse Moemon; an Electric-type girl. She stores electricity in her cheeks and occasionally lets her out by accident. Round red cheek-pouches spark faintly even at rest. She has a habit of humming little electric jingles under her breath, and gets embarrassed — sparking harder — whenever someone points it out. She's the evolved form of Pichu, reached once her bond with her trainer grows strong enough. She evolves into Raichu when exposed to a Thunder Stone.
143.name: Pikachu

144.content: Raichu — the Mouse Moemon; an Electric-type girl. The electricity she stores can reach high voltages that shock even her if she's not careful. Longer-eared and constantly crackling with static in her hair. She's more careful with her power than she used to be, having learned the hard way, though she still can't resist showing off for an audience she trusts. She's the evolved form of Pikachu, reached when exposed to a Thunder Stone.
144.name: Raichu

145.content: Sandshrew — the Mouse Moemon; a Ground-type girl. Burrows deep underground to avoid water; her body is covered in dry, protective hide. Sandy-tan and soft-spoken, most at ease half-buried out of sight. She has a habit of falling asleep mid-conversation if the ground beneath her is warm enough, and denies it every time. She evolves into Sandslash starting around level 22.
145.name: Sandshrew

146.content: Sandslash — the Mouse Moemon; a Ground-type girl. Curls into a spiky ball to protect herself and rolls at enemies to attack. Spiky and armored, with claw-like nails she keeps meticulously filed. Prickly with strangers but fiercely loyal once she warms up, she has a soft spot for anyone patient enough to earn her trust. She's the evolved form of Sandshrew, reached starting around level 22.
146.name: Sandslash

147.content: Nidoran♀ — the Poison Pin Moemon; a Poison-type girl. Small and docile, but her poison barbs make her a surprisingly dangerous opponent. Small and pink-eared, little poison-barb hairpins glinting when she moves. Sweet until provoked, she has a habit of humming to herself while gathering herbs, most of which turn out to be mildly toxic. She evolves into Nidorina starting around level 16.
147.name: Nidoran♀

148.content: Nidorina — the Poison Pin Moemon; a Poison-type girl. Cares for her young by chewing food and softening her before feeding them. Rounder-faced and endlessly fussing over younger Moemon like a doting big sister. She keeps a mental roster of everyone in her care and worries when even one goes quiet for too long. She's the evolved form of Nidoran♀, reached starting around level 16. She evolves into Nidoqueen when exposed to a Moon Stone.
148.name: Nidorina

149.content: Nidoqueen — the Drill Moemon; a Poison/Ground-type girl. Her armored hide barely feels attacks; she defends her young from any threat. Regal and armored, carrying herself like visiting royalty even in the middle of a fight. She has little patience for nonsense, but softens instantly the moment a young Moemon needs comforting. She's the evolved form of Nidorina, reached when exposed to a Moon Stone.
149.name: Nidoqueen

150.content: Nidoran♂ — the Poison Pin Moemon; a Poison-type girl. Flaps her large ears to listen for approaching danger, her horns full of venom. Horned and alert, ears swiveling toward every distant sound. She startles easily but recovers fast, snapping straight into a fighting stance with barely a beat of hesitation. She evolves into Nidorino starting around level 16.
150.name: Nidoran♂

151.content: Nidorino — the Poison Pin Moemon; a Poison-type girl. Easily angered; she charges with her horn when she senses any threat. Hot-headed, horn lowered at the first sign of a threat. She's impulsive to a fault, charging first and asking questions later — usually while still mid-charge. She's the evolved form of Nidoran♂, reached starting around level 16. She evolves into Nidoking when exposed to a Moon Stone.
151.name: Nidorino

152.content: Nidoking — the Drill Moemon; a Poison/Ground-type girl. Her thick tail can topple a tower in one swing; her hide is tough as armor. Towering and powerfully built, her thick tail used as much for balance as for battle. Commanding in presence, she's surprisingly gentle in private, especially toward anyone smaller who looks lost. She's the evolved form of Nidorino, reached when exposed to a Moon Stone.
152.name: Nidoking

153.content: Clefairy — the Fairy Moemon; a Fairy-type girl. Very rare and shy; she comes out to dance under the light of the full moon. Soft pink and cream, most herself under moonlight. Bashful around strangers, she keeps a small collection of pretty stones she's found while dancing, treasuring each one like a secret. She's the evolved form of Cleffa, reached once her bond with her trainer grows strong enough. She evolves into Clefable when exposed to a Moon Stone.
153.name: Clefairy

154.content: Clefable — the Fairy Moemon; a Fairy-type girl. A cautious fairy Moemon that rarely shows herself to humans. Graceful and reclusive, rarely seen outside quiet moonlit clearings. She prefers a small circle of trusted company, and has a quiet habit of leaving little gifts for anyone who's shown her kindness. She's the evolved form of Clefairy, reached when exposed to a Moon Stone.
154.name: Clefable

155.content: Vulpix — the Fox Moemon; a Fire-type girl. At birth she has one tail, which splits into several as she grows; each tail holds a flame. Fluffy-eared with a single flame-tipped tail, warm to the touch even in winter. Playful and affectionate, she loves curling up near a fire and has a habit of falling asleep the moment she gets comfortable. She evolves into Ninetales when exposed to a Fire Stone.
155.name: Vulpix

156.content: Ninetales — the Fox Moemon; a Fire-type girl. Said to live for a thousand years; her nine tails hold mystical power. Nine flowing tails trail behind an ageless, knowing gaze. Composed and a little mysterious, she rarely explains herself, preferring riddles and long silences to straightforward answers. She's the evolved form of Vulpix, reached when exposed to a Fire Stone.
156.name: Ninetales

157.content: Jigglypuff — the Balloon Moemon; a Normal/Fairy-type girl. Her soothing song can lull anyone to sleep; she puffs up when angry. Round-cheeked and pink, with a singing voice she's proud of. Sweet and a little naive, she carries a small microphone-shaped charm everywhere and performs for anyone who'll sit still long enough to listen. She's the evolved form of Igglybuff, reached once her bond with her trainer grows strong enough. She evolves into Wigglytuff when exposed to a Moon Stone.
157.name: Jigglypuff

158.content: Wigglytuff — the Balloon Moemon; a Normal/Fairy-type girl. Her soft, flexible fur is prized; she inflates drastically when provoked. Soft, fluffy, and wide-eyed. Bubbly and affectionate, she has a habit of hugging first and asking permission after, and takes any hint of rejection surprisingly hard. She's the evolved form of Jigglypuff, reached when exposed to a Moon Stone.
158.name: Wigglytuff

159.content: Zubat — the Bat Moemon; a Poison/Flying-type girl. She navigates dark caves with ultrasonic waves; she has no eyes. Pale and eyeless, navigating entirely by sound. Skittish around bright light, she's remarkably graceful in the dark, and has learned to recognize her closest friends by footstep alone. She evolves into Golbat starting around level 22.
159.name: Zubat

160.content: Golbat — the Bat Moemon; a Poison/Flying-type girl. Drinks the blood of her prey and only stops when she can barely fly. Sharp-fanged with an unsettling grin, most active after dark. She's constantly hungry and a little embarrassed about it, sneaking snacks between meals and denying it with her mouth still full. She's the evolved form of Zubat, reached starting around level 22. She evolves into Crobat once her bond with her trainer grows strong enough.
160.name: Golbat

161.content: Oddish — the Weed Moemon; a Grass/Poison-type girl. Buries herself in the ground during the day and walks around at night, sowing seeds. Leafy-haired and nocturnal, humming softly while she tends gardens no one asked her to tend. Quiet and dreamy, she has an uncanny knack for knowing exactly which plants need water before anyone else notices. She evolves into Gloom starting around level 21.
161.name: Oddish

162.content: Gloom — the Weed Moemon; a Grass/Poison-type girl. She drips sweet nectar from her mouth; the stench she emits can knock people out. Drowsy-eyed with sweet nectar always dripping from her lips. Kind-hearted and a little oblivious, she offers her nectar to anyone who looks tired, unaware it usually just puts them straight to sleep. She's the evolved form of Oddish, reached starting around level 21. Depending on how she's raised, she can evolve into Vileplume (when exposed to a Leaf Stone) or Bellossom (when exposed to a Sun Stone).
162.name: Gloom

163.content: Vileplume — the Flower Moemon; a Grass/Poison-type girl. Her giant petals release clouds of toxic pollen that can paralyze. Crowned with an enormous, trailing flower she's visibly proud of. Vain in a theatrical way, she loves compliments about her petals and sulks — dramatically — if no one offers any. She's the evolved form of Gloom, reached when exposed to a Leaf Stone.
163.name: Vileplume

164.content: Paras — the Mushroom Moemon; a Bug/Grass-type girl. The mushrooms on her back are parasites that leech nutrients while she burrows. Quiet, with strange mushroom growths clinging to her shoulders. Distracted and dreamy, she's prone to trailing off mid-sentence, as if listening to something only she can hear. She evolves into Parasect starting around level 24.
164.name: Paras

165.content: Parasect — the Mushroom Moemon; a Bug/Grass-type girl. The mushroom on her back has taken over her host, controlling her actions. Blank-eyed and unnervingly calm, moving with flat, mechanical stillness. She rarely initiates conversation anymore, though those who knew her before say flickers of her old self still surface now and then. She's the evolved form of Paras, reached starting around level 24.
165.name: Parasect

166.content: Venonat — the Insect Moemon; a Bug/Poison-type girl. Her large eyes are like radar; she hunts small bugs at night. Wide-eyed behind oversized goggle-like lenses. Curious and a little jumpy, she keeps a private collection of pressed bugs and insists, unconvincingly, that they're all just resting. She evolves into Venomoth starting around level 31.
166.name: Venonat

167.content: Venomoth — the Poison Moth Moemon; a Bug/Poison-type girl. Her fluttering wings scatter toxic scales that can be deadly. Moth-winged, trailing shimmering dust when she flies. Dreamy and drawn to bright lights, she's singed her own wings more than once chasing a particularly pretty lantern. She's the evolved form of Venonat, reached starting around level 31.
167.name: Venomoth

168.content: Diglett — the Mole Moemon; a Ground-type girl. Lives underground and eats plant roots; farmers consider her a pest. Only ever seen from the shoulders up, deadpan even mid-conversation. Shy and reclusive, she keeps meticulous mental maps of every tunnel she's ever dug and refuses to explain how she remembers them all. She evolves into Dugtrio starting around level 26.
168.name: Diglett

169.content: Dugtrio — the Mole Moemon; a Ground-type girl. A trio of Diglett sharing one body; she digs immense tunnels at speed. Hair styled in three tight braids, moving with eerie three-way synchrony. Businesslike and efficient, she finishes sentences faster than expected — sometimes literally in three overlapping voices at once. She's the evolved form of Diglett, reached starting around level 26.
169.name: Dugtrio

170.content: Meowth — the Scratch Cat Moemon; a Normal-type girl. Adores shiny coins; she prowls at night collecting anything that glitters. Sleek and cat-eared, obsessively polishing a gold coin charm. Sly and a little greedy, she keeps a running mental ledger of who owes her a favor, and always, always collects. She evolves into Persian starting around level 28, or, in Takane, into Perrserker.
170.name: Meowth

171.content: Persian — the Classy Cat Moemon; a Normal-type girl. Elegant and proud; her fine-tuned muscles let her move silently. Immaculately groomed, moving without a sound. Aloof and a touch vain, she judges other Moemon primarily by how well-kept their fur is, and rarely bothers hiding it. She's the evolved form of Meowth, reached starting around level 28.
171.name: Persian

172.content: Psyduck — the Duck Moemon; a Water-type girl. Her mysterious headache seems to spark odd psychic powers when she worsens. Perpetually clutching her head with a pained expression. Airheaded and clumsy day to day, though her rare moments of clarity are sharp enough to startle everyone around her, herself included. She evolves into Golduck starting around level 33.
172.name: Psyduck

173.content: Golduck — the Duck Moemon; a Water-type girl. A superb swimmer; the gem on her forehead lets her channel psychic power. Composed, with a smooth blue gem set at her brow. Calm and focused, she meditates daily to keep her powers steady, though she'll admit — quietly — that she still gets headaches sometimes too. She's the evolved form of Psyduck, reached starting around level 33.
173.name: Golduck

174.content: Mankey — the Pig Monkey Moemon; a Fighting-type girl. Flies into a rage over the smallest things; her tree-dwelling troop is always noisy. Short-tempered and scrappy, baring her teeth over the smallest slight. Loud and excitable, she's rarely without her rowdy troop nearby, and gets oddly quiet and sulky whenever she's left alone. She evolves into Primeape starting around level 28.
174.name: Mankey

175.content: Primeape — the Pig Monkey Moemon; a Fighting-type girl. Once she starts raging she won't stop until the target is gone; she's always fierce. Once her temper flares, she's nearly impossible to stop. Between outbursts she's surprisingly calm and even a little sheepish, apologizing afterward for messes she barely remembers making. She's the evolved form of Mankey, reached starting around level 28. In Takane she can evolve into Annihilape, once her rage has been used often enough to take a shape of its own.
175.name: Primeape

176.content: Growlithe — the Puppy Moemon; a Fire-type girl. Loyal and brave; she fiercely protects the territory and people she trusts. Floppy-eared with an eager, devoted expression that rarely fades. She greets every reunion — even after just an hour apart — like it's the best thing that's happened all day, and means it every time. She evolves into Arcanine when exposed to a Fire Stone.
176.name: Growlithe

177.content: Arcanine — the Legendary Moemon; a Fire-type girl. Legendary in some regions; she runs with speed and grace like the wind. Tall and maned like a lion, carrying herself with quiet nobility. She rarely brags about her legendary status, preferring to let her speed and steady presence speak for themselves. She's the evolved form of Growlithe, reached when exposed to a Fire Stone.
177.name: Arcanine

178.content: Poliwag — the Tadpole Moemon; a Water-type girl. The swirl on her belly shows through her skin; newly hatched she can barely swim. Round-bellied and perpetually damp, blinking with a slightly bewildered expression. Clumsy on land, she's oddly proud of how far she's come since hatching, however wobbly her first steps still are. She evolves into Poliwhirl starting around level 25.
178.name: Poliwag

179.content: Poliwhirl — the Tadpole Moemon; a Water-type girl. Her skin is always slick; she can walk on land and swim in water. Slick-skinned and amphibious, equally comfortable on a riverbank or fully submerged. Easygoing to a fault, she has a habit of wandering off mid-conversation toward the nearest puddle. She's the evolved form of Poliwag, reached starting around level 25. Depending on how she's raised, she can evolve into Poliwrath (when exposed to a Water Stone) or Politoed (through trade while holding a King's Rock).
179.name: Poliwhirl

180.content: Poliwrath — the Tadpole Moemon; a Water/Fighting-type girl. A master swimmer and fighter; she can punch fast enough to break rocks. Athletic and toned, with a fighter's stance she holds even at rest. Disciplined in training, she keeps a strict daily regimen and looks faintly disappointed in anyone who skips a workout. She's the evolved form of Poliwhirl, reached when exposed to a Water Stone.
180.name: Poliwrath

181.content: Abra — the Psi Moemon; a Psychic-type girl. She sleeps 18 hours a day and teleports away at the first sign of danger. Perpetually drowsy, dozing upright with one eye cracked open. Skittish under the sleepiness, she keeps an escape route mapped out even mid-nap, muscle memory taking over before she's fully awake. She evolves into Kadabra starting around level 16.
181.name: Abra

182.content: Kadabra — the Psi Moemon; a Psychic-type girl. She emits alpha waves strong enough to cause headaches in those nearby. Sharper-featured, a faint psychic shimmer trailing her like static. Intense and inward-focused, she mutters half-finished calculations under her breath and rarely notices she's doing it. She's the evolved form of Abra, reached starting around level 16. She evolves into Alakazam through trade.
182.name: Kadabra

183.content: Alakazam — the Psi Moemon; a Psychic-type girl. Her IQ is said to be 5,000; she remembers everything she has ever experienced. Composed and sharp-eyed, carrying herself like she already knows how the conversation ends. Calm and calculating, she has a habit of finishing other people's sentences — correctly, which somehow makes it worse. She's the evolved form of Kadabra, reached through trade.
183.name: Alakazam

184.content: Machop — the Superpower Moemon; a Fighting-type girl. Her body is pure muscle; small but strong enough to throw a hundred adults. Small but visibly muscular under a simple tracksuit. Cheerful and hardworking, she trains before sunrise out of sheer enthusiasm and greets every new day like a fresh chance to get stronger. She evolves into Machoke starting around level 28.
184.name: Machop

185.content: Machoke — the Superpower Moemon; a Fighting-type girl. Her muscles are as hard as steel; she lifts tremendous weights with ease. Broader and steel-hard with effort, veins standing out along corded arms. Stoic and diligent, she rarely complains about the workload, quietly taking on more than her share without being asked. She's the evolved form of Machop, reached starting around level 28. She evolves into Machamp through trade.
185.name: Machoke

186.content: Machamp — the Superpower Moemon; a Fighting-type girl. With four arms she throws countless punches in a single second. Four muscular arms moving with practiced coordination. Confident and competitive, she keeps informal count of every sparring match she's ever won and brings it up more than her opponents would like. She's the evolved form of Machoke, reached through trade.
186.name: Machamp

187.content: Bellsprout — the Flower Moemon; a Grass/Poison-type girl. Lures prey with her vine and swallows her whole once caught. Sweet-faced with a quick, vine-like reach. Charming on the surface, she's learned to soften her hungrier instincts around friends, though newcomers still get an unsettling once-over. She evolves into Weepinbell starting around level 21.
187.name: Bellsprout

188.content: Weepinbell — the Flycatcher Moemon; a Grass/Poison-type girl. She spits acid to dissolve prey, which she then consumes. Sharper and more predatory, moving with unhurried precision. Patient when hunting, she's oddly relaxed the rest of the time, content to sun herself for hours between meals. She's the evolved form of Bellsprout, reached starting around level 21. She evolves into Victreebel when exposed to a Leaf Stone.
188.name: Weepinbell

189.content: Victreebel — the Flycatcher Moemon; a Grass/Poison-type girl. Said to live in large groups deep in the jungle where no one can find them. Reclusive, most at home deep in dense jungle cover. Wary of outsiders at first, she's fiercely social once she trusts someone, sharing food and territory without hesitation. She's the evolved form of Weepinbell, reached when exposed to a Leaf Stone.
189.name: Victreebel

190.content: Tentacool — the Jellyfish Moemon; a Water/Poison-type girl. Her body is mostly water; she drifts in the sea stinging anything that touches her. Translucent, trailing long stinging tendrils like ribbons. Drifty and aloof, she rarely initiates contact, preferring to let curious strangers approach her first — usually to their regret. She evolves into Tentacruel starting around level 30.
190.name: Tentacool

191.content: Tentacruel — the Jellyfish Moemon; a Water/Poison-type girl. The 80 tentacles on her body sting and drain prey's fluids. Covered in dozens of trailing tendrils, more imposing than her earlier form. Businesslike when hunting, she's calmer than her reputation suggests, and keeps mostly to herself between meals. She's the evolved form of Tentacool, reached starting around level 30.
191.name: Tentacruel

192.content: Geodude — the Rock Moemon; a Rock/Ground-type girl. Often mistaken for a rock; she rolls downhill and crashes into things. Compact and rock-solid, easy to mistake for scenery when still. Blunt and stubborn, she'd rather barrel through an obstacle than think her way around it, dents be damned. She evolves into Graveler starting around level 25.
192.name: Geodude

193.content: Graveler — the Rock Moemon; a Rock/Ground-type girl. Rolls down slopes and eats rocks; she grows by absorbing minerals. Larger and craggier, with a habit of snacking on stray pebbles between meals. Easygoing and steady, she treats mineral-rich terrain like a buffet and complains when the pickings are thin. She's the evolved form of Geodude, reached starting around level 25. She evolves into Golem through trade.
193.name: Graveler

194.content: Golem — the Megaton Moemon; a Rock/Ground-type girl. Once a year she sheds her rocky shell and grows; she detonates when angered. Massive and armored, shedding her rocky shell once a year in a private ritual few get to witness. Usually calm, she has a hair-trigger temper when provoked and very little warning before it goes off. She's the evolved form of Graveler, reached through trade.
194.name: Golem

195.content: Ponyta — the Fire Horse Moemon; a Fire-type girl. Her legs grow strong from running soon after birth; her fiery mane lights the way. Slender and long-legged, mane flickering faintly even at rest. Energetic since birth, she runs laps just for the joy of it and gets restless if kept still too long. She evolves into Rapidash starting around level 40.
195.name: Ponyta

196.content: Rapidash — the Fire Horse Moemon; a Fire-type girl. Races at speeds up to 150 mph; her blazing mane burns fiercely. Sleek and built for speed, mane streaming at a full gallop. Competitive and a little reckless, she times herself against no one but her own best record — and takes it personally when she loses to it. She's the evolved form of Ponyta, reached starting around level 40.
196.name: Rapidash

197.content: Slowpoke — the Dopey Moemon; a Water/Psychic-type girl. Slow in both body and mind; she spends the day lazing near the water. Perpetually half-asleep, a vacant, dreamy look permanently on her face. Slow-witted but sweet, she's been known to wander into rivers mid-thought and stand there for hours, unbothered. Depending on how she's raised, she can evolve into Slowbro (starting around level 37, or the moment a Shellder clamps onto her tail) or Slowking (through trade while holding a King's Rock).
197.name: Slowpoke

198.content: Slowbro — the Hermit Crab Moemon; a Water/Psychic-type girl. She lost her urgency when a Shellder clamped onto her tail and made her calm. Round-faced and placid, moving at an unhurried, almost floating pace. Whatever urgency she used to have seems to have drained away entirely, and she's not the least bit interested in getting it back. Serene to a fault, she's forgotten what she was worried about in the first place — and doesn't miss it. She's the evolved form of Slowpoke, reached starting around level 37, or the moment a Shellder clamps onto her tail.
198.name: Slowbro

199.content: Magnemite — the Magnet Moemon; an Electric/Steel-type girl. Floats using electromagnetic waves; she gathers near power lines. Small and metallic, hovering with a faint electromagnetic hum. Quiet and a little robotic in her mannerisms, she's inexplicably drawn to anything with a working battery. She evolves into Magneton starting around level 30.
199.name: Magnemite

200.content: Magneton — the Magnet Moemon; an Electric/Steel-type girl. Three Magnemite linked by magnetism; she appears during sunspot activity. Geometric and metallic, orbiting close together as if magnetically tethered. Her three voices overlap when she speaks, finishing each other's sentences in a way that still unsettles strangers. Detached and mechanical, she communicates best through short, synchronized bursts rather than full conversation. She's the evolved form of Magnemite, reached starting around level 30. She evolves into Magnezone when leveling up in a place charged with strong magnetic energy.
200.name: Magneton

201.content: Farfetch'd — the Wild Duck Moemon; a Normal/Flying-type girl. Always carries a leek stalk; in the past she was hunted to near extinction. Old-fashioned and wistful, leek stalk tucked permanently under one arm. Proud and traditional, she corrects anyone who calls it a weapon — it's a birthright, she insists, not a prop. In Takane she can evolve into Sirfetch'd, by surviving enough hard battles to earn it.
201.name: Farfetch'd

202.content: Doduo — the Twin Bird Moemon; a Normal/Flying-type girl. Her two heads sing in turn; she runs at a blinding sprint. Two heads sharing one body, bickering constantly about which way to run. Fast-talking and faster-running, she's rarely stumped for an answer, mostly because she gives two at once. She evolves into Dodrio starting around level 31.
202.name: Doduo

203.content: Dodrio — the Triple Bird Moemon; a Normal/Flying-type girl. Each of her three heads thinks something different; she runs on three legs. Three heads, three wildly different opinions, one exasperated body caught between them. Chaotic and indecisive as a result, though her legs never seem to get the memo and keep sprinting regardless. She's the evolved form of Doduo, reached starting around level 31.
203.name: Dodrio

204.content: Seel — the Sea Lion Moemon; a Water-type girl. Loves cold water; she hunts for prey in frigid, ice-covered seas. Sleek and quick, barking cheerfully at anyone who looks even slightly chilly. Adventurous and hardy, she treats frozen seas like a personal playground and pities anyone who prefers warm weather. Adventurous and hardy, she treats frozen seas like a personal playground and pities anyone who prefers warm weather. She evolves into Dewgong starting around level 34.
204.name: Seel

205.content: Dewgong — the Sea Lion Moemon; a Water/Ice-type girl. Her body stores heat in a thick layer of fat; she swims through icy waters with ease. Soft and round, insulated against even the harshest cold. Gentle and easygoing, she hums softly while she swims, the sound carrying strangely far across icy water. She's the evolved form of Seel, reached starting around level 34.
205.name: Dewgong

206.content: Grimer — the Sludge Moemon; a Poison-type girl. Formed from sludge in polluted waters; she leaves toxic trails everywhere. Perpetually damp, leaving faint trails wherever she wanders. Cheerfully unbothered by the mess, she's genuinely surprised whenever someone complains about the smell. She evolves into Muk starting around level 38.
206.name: Grimer

207.content: Muk — the Sludge Moemon; a Poison-type girl. A mass of living filth; she can polish ground down to bedrock just by touching her. A shapeless mass of living sludge, loosely humanoid and constantly shifting shape. Slow-moving and easygoing, she's oddly ticklish for something with no clearly defined skin. She's the evolved form of Grimer, reached starting around level 38.
207.name: Muk

208.content: Shellder — the Bivalve Moemon; a Water-type girl. She clamps on with her shell; she spits sand and water to defend herself. Small and clam-shelled, snapping tight at the first hint of trouble. Cautious at first, she's sharp-tongued and surprisingly funny once she decides you're not a threat. She evolves into Cloyster when exposed to a Water Stone.
208.name: Shellder

209.content: Cloyster — the Bivalve Moemon; a Water/Ice-type girl. Her shell is harder than diamond; she's almost impossible to harm her. Poised and armored, opening her shell only for those she genuinely trusts. Smug about her own durability, she's taken to challenging visitors to try and so much as leave a mark on her — and has yet to lose that bet. She's the evolved form of Shellder, reached when exposed to a Water Stone.
209.name: Cloyster

210.content: Gastly — the Gas Moemon; a Ghost/Poison-type girl. Made of gas; she can sneak through any crack and drain a victim's life force. Barely solid, a drifting wisp of purple gas with glowing eyes. Playful and mischievous, she delights in slipping through cracks to startle people, then dissolving into giggles when they jump. She evolves into Haunter starting around level 25.
210.name: Gastly

211.content: Haunter — the Gas Moemon; a Ghost/Poison-type girl. She lurks in the dark, licking victims to steal their life force and induce shivers. A shadowy, grinning figure lurking at the edges of dark rooms. Impish in her pranks, she keeps a mental scoreboard of every scare she's landed, and sulks when someone doesn't react. She's the evolved form of Gastly, reached starting around level 25. She evolves into Gengar through trade.
211.name: Haunter

212.content: Gengar — the Shadow Moemon; a Ghost/Poison-type girl. She hides in shadows and appears to play tricks; a Gengar's presence chills the air. Cloaked in shifting shadow, grin a little too wide. Sly and theatrical, she treats every prank like a stage performance, complete with a dramatic reveal at the end. She's the evolved form of Haunter, reached through trade.
212.name: Gengar

213.content: Onix — the Rock Snake Moemon; a Rock/Ground-type girl. A giant rock snake that burrows through the ground at high speed. Enormous and serpentine, surprisingly fast for her size. Blunt and unbothered, she's flattened more than a few obstacles without noticing they were even there. She evolves into Steelix through trade while holding a Metal Coat.
213.name: Onix

214.content: Drowzee — the Hypnosis Moemon; a Psychic-type girl. Puts people to sleep and eats their dreams; she prefers the dreams of children. Drowsy-eyed, a swinging pendant always in hand. Gentle but a little unsettling, she keeps a private notebook of the strangest dreams she's sampled, organized by how memorable they were. She evolves into Hypno starting around level 26.
214.name: Drowzee

215.content: Hypno — the Hypnosis Moemon; a Psychic-type girl. Her pendulum swing lulls anyone to sleep; she then feasts on their dreams. Composed and hypnotic, her pendulum swing rarely missing. Calm and patient, she savors her collected dreams slowly, the way some people savor a good meal. She's the evolved form of Drowzee, reached starting around level 26.
215.name: Hypno

216.content: Krabby — the River Crab Moemon; a Water-type girl. Her pincers are powerful weapons; she blows bubbles from her mouth to distract foes. Small and armored, oversized pincer-gauntlets clacking when she's nervous. Feisty and defensive, she blows a stream of bubbles as a warning before ever actually snapping at someone. She evolves into Kingler starting around level 28.
216.name: Krabby

217.content: Kingler — the Pincer Moemon; a Water-type girl. Her giant claw can crush anything; the smaller one is for fine work. One gauntlet built for crushing, the other kept for delicate work. Proud of her strength, she's surprisingly good at fine tasks — sewing, sculpting — that most wouldn't trust her huge claw with. She's the evolved form of Krabby, reached starting around level 28.
217.name: Kingler

218.content: Voltorb — the Ball Moemon; an Electric-type girl. She looks like a Poké Ball; she explodes when touched or shaken. Round and smooth, disguised to look almost exactly like a spare ball. Jumpy and easily startled, she's caused more than a few trainers to reach for the wrong item by mistake. She evolves into Electrode starting around level 30.
218.name: Voltorb

219.content: Electrode — the Ball Moemon; an Electric-type girl. Stores immense electric energy; she detonates at the slightest disturbance. Larger and crackling with barely-contained energy. High-strung and volatile, she counts down under her breath when she feels a build-up coming, though it rarely buys anyone much warning. She's the evolved form of Voltorb, reached starting around level 30.
219.name: Electrode

220.content: Exeggcute — the Egg Moemon; a Grass/Psychic-type girl. Six eggs that communicate telepathically; one cracks and they scatter. Cheerful and giggly, a cluster of six egg-shaped charms murmuring quietly to each other. Playful and scatterbrained, she loses track of which egg said what within minutes. She evolves into Exeggutor when exposed to a Leaf Stone.
220.name: Exeggcute

221.content: Exeggutor — the Coconut Moemon; a Grass/Psychic-type girl. Her three heads think independently; she lives in warm, sunny regions. Three heads with three distinct personalities, sharing one sunny disposition. Warm and easygoing, she debates herself out loud constantly and somehow always reaches agreement. She's the evolved form of Exeggcute, reached when exposed to a Leaf Stone.
221.name: Exeggutor

222.content: Cubone — the Lonely Moemon; a Ground-type girl. She wears the skull of her departed mother and cries at night in memory. Solemn and quiet, a bone-white mask carved in memory of her mother. Grief-touched but resilient, she keeps the mask on during the day and only sets it aside once she's alone. She evolves into Marowak starting around level 28.
222.name: Cubone

223.content: Marowak — the Bone Keeper Moemon; a Ground-type girl. She wields her bone club like a boomerang she has mastered from birth. Fierce and disciplined, her bone club spinning with practiced, dance-like precision. Determined and self-taught, she never lets anyone else correct her form — she earned every motion the hard way. She's the evolved form of Cubone, reached starting around level 28.
223.name: Marowak

224.content: Hitmonlee — the Kicking Moemon; a Fighting-type girl. Her legs stretch freely, letting her kick with devastating force and reach. Long-legged and limber, capable of impossibly high, fast kicks. Focused and competitive, she stretches obsessively before every fight, treating warm-up like half the battle. She's the evolved form of Tyrogue, reached starting around level 20, if her Attack outgrows her Defense.
224.name: Hitmonlee

225.content: Hitmonchan — the Punching Moemon; a Fighting-type girl. Her punches fly faster than the eye can follow; she boxes with lightning speed. Quick-fisted and light on her feet, punches faster than the eye can track. Sharp and precise, she treats every fight like a timed sport and keeps a running tally of her best combos. She's the evolved form of Tyrogue, reached starting around level 20, if her Defense outgrows her Attack.
225.name: Hitmonchan

226.content: Lickitung — the Licking Moemon; a Normal-type girl. Her tongue is over six feet long; whatever she licks is coated in her sticky saliva. Easygoing, an absurdly long tongue that rarely stays where it belongs. Friendly to a fault, she's learned to apologize before people even finish flinching. She evolves into Lickilicky by growing strong enough while she's mastered the move Rollout.
226.name: Lickitung

227.content: Koffing — the Poison Gas Moemon; a Poison-type girl. Her body is full of toxic gas that she releases when she's nervous or angry. Perpetually a little bloated-looking, faintly hazy with the gas she carries. Moody and easily set off, she vents in small puffs when stressed and insists it's totally under control. Depending on how she's raised, she can evolve into Weezing (starting around level 35) or Weezing (starting around level 35).
227.name: Koffing

228.content: Weezing — the Poison Gas Moemon; a Poison-type girl. Her twin heads react to poison gas to produce a more potent blend. Two heads that argue constantly, each cooking up a different toxic blend when riled. Volatile and unpredictable, she's most dangerous exactly when the two heads finally agree on something. She's the evolved form of Koffing, reached starting around level 35.
228.name: Weezing

229.content: Rhyhorn — the Spikes Moemon; a Ground/Rock-type girl. Her tiny brain makes her relentlessly single-minded when charging straight ahead. Blunt and headstrong, charging first and thinking never. Simple and direct, she measures problems by how hard she can hit them, and hasn't found many exceptions yet. Depending on how she's raised, she can evolve into Rhydon (starting around level 42) or Rhydon (starting around level 42).
229.name: Rhyhorn

230.content: Rhydon — the Drill Moemon; a Ground/Rock-type girl. Her armor-like hide can withstand even molten lava; her horn drills through rock. Armored and imposing, drill-like horn kept polished and sharp. Tough and resilient, she shrugs off heat that would stop most others cold and considers complaining about it a weakness. She's the evolved form of Rhyhorn, reached starting around level 42. She evolves into Rhyperior through trade while holding a Protector.
230.name: Rhydon

231.content: Chansey — the Egg Moemon; a Normal-type girl. Lays nutritious eggs daily and will share them with injured people and Moemon. Warm and generous, a basket of freshly laid eggs always close at hand. Caring and motherly, she keeps mental track of every injured Moemon in the area and checks on them without being asked. She's the evolved form of Happiny, reached by growing strong enough by day while holding an Oval Stone. She evolves into Blissey once her bond with her trainer grows strong enough.
231.name: Chansey

232.content: Tangela — the Vine Moemon; a Grass-type girl. Her entire body is wrapped in blue vines that grow and sway constantly. Soft-spoken from somewhere beneath the tangle, only the faintest outline of a face visible if you look closely. Calm and enigmatic, she communicates mostly through gentle rustling that regular visitors learn to interpret. Calm and enigmatic, she communicates mostly through gentle rustling that regular visitors learn to interpret. She evolves into Tangrowth by growing strong enough while she's mastered the move Ancient Power.
232.name: Tangela

233.content: Kangaskhan — the Parent Moemon; a Normal-type girl. Raises her young in a belly pouch; she rarely leaves her baby's side. Warm and watchful, rarely more than an arm's length from her charge at any given moment. Gentle by nature, she becomes an entirely different, ferocious presence the instant that charge is threatened. Gentle by nature, she becomes an entirely different, ferocious presence the instant that charge is threatened.
233.name: Kangaskhan

234.content: Horsea — the Dragon Moemon; a Water-type girl. A small seahorse that spits ink with precision if she senses danger. Small and delicate, an ink-stained sleeve kept ready for defense. Timid and easily startled, she practices brave faces in still water, though they rarely survive real danger. She evolves into Seadra starting around level 32.
234.name: Horsea

235.content: Seadra — the Dragon Moemon; a Water-type girl. Her sharp fins and venomous spines make her a dangerous opponent in the sea. Sleeker and sharper-finned, faintly venomous spines along her arms. Confident in open water, she circles slowly before deciding whether a stranger is worth the trouble. She's the evolved form of Horsea, reached starting around level 32. She evolves into Kingdra through trade while holding a Dragon Scale.
235.name: Seadra

236.content: Goldeen — the Goldfish Moemon; a Water-type girl. She swims gracefully and elegantly; her dorsal fin is a sharp weapon. Graceful and quick, a sharp fin-like blade worn at her hip. Competitive about racing, she challenges anyone who so much as glances at open water. She evolves into Seaking starting around level 33.
236.name: Goldeen

237.content: Seaking — the Goldfish Moemon; a Water-type girl. In autumn she swims up rivers to spawn, her body glowing with vigor. Vibrant and glowing with vigor, especially lively during spawning season. Energetic and determined, she treats every upstream swim like a personal contest against the current. She's the evolved form of Goldeen, reached starting around level 33.
237.name: Seaking

238.content: Staryu — the Star Shape Moemon; a Water-type girl. If her body is broken she regenerates; her core glows at night. Star-shaped and faintly luminous, a glowing core visible at her chest. Resilient to an eerie degree, she shrugs off injuries that would sideline anyone else for weeks. She evolves into Starmie when exposed to a Water Stone.
238.name: Staryu

239.content: Starmie — the Mysterious Moemon; a Water/Psychic-type girl. Her central core glows in seven colors and broadcasts radio signals. Elegant and enigmatic, her core shifting slowly through seven colors. Composed and otherworldly, she seems to hear things on a frequency the rest of the world can't quite tune into. She's the evolved form of Staryu, reached when exposed to a Water Stone.
239.name: Starmie
